title: Optional IBKR data provider — non-blocking review follow-ups
description: Non-blocking findings from pr-reviewer's full review of PR #190 (backend-ibkr-data-provider), tracked here per CLAUDE.md's autonomous-pipeline rule so they aren't lost once that PR merges.

checklist.step: app.api.dependencies.get_ibkr_provider() constructs a brand-new IBKRProvider (closed at the end of every request) on every dependency resolution, so IBKRProvider's in-memory scanner-params TTL cache and 1-req/sec run_scanner throttle never persist across requests. This is currently dormant (no route consumes get_ibkr_provider yet) but whoever builds the first consuming endpoint needs to choose a longer-lived instance (e.g. a module-level singleton, or move the cache/throttle state to a shared store) rather than assume the per-request FastAPI dependency already provides IBKR-rate-limit protection.

docs/architecture/Backend.md §3's 'Key Dependencies' table still lists `httpx` with the purpose 'via FastAPI TestClient | API integration tests' only -- it wasn't updated to also reflect that `httpx` is now a main/production runtime dependency (app/data/ibkr_provider.py's `IBKRProvider` performs real HTTP calls with it, not just tests). Update the §3 table row to mention IBKRProvider's production use alongside the existing TestClient-testing purpose.

app.api.dependencies.get_ibkr_provider()'s lazy singleton init (`if _ibkr_provider_singleton is None: _ibkr_provider_singleton = IBKRProvider(...)`) is a check-then-set on a plain module-level global with no lock, and FastAPI runs sync dependency generators in a worker thread pool -- two concurrent first-requests can both observe None and each construct their own IBKRProvider (each with independent scanner-params cache / run_scanner throttle state and its own un-closed httpx.Client), silently defeating exactly the cross-request rate-limit protection this singleton was introduced for. Consider a thread-safe lazy-init instead of hand-rolled double-checked locking -- e.g. an `@lru_cache(maxsize=1)`-wrapped factory, matching `get_settings()`'s own already-thread-safe pattern (backend/app/config.py) rather than reinventing it. Currently dormant (no route consumes get_ibkr_provider yet), found during PR #190's re-review (pr-reviewer, code-review skill sub-agent).

The module-global `_ibkr_provider_singleton` has no autouse test fixture resetting it between tests -- only the two tests that directly exercise get_ibkr_provider() remember to `monkeypatch.setattr(..., None)` first. A future test that reaches this dependency indirectly (e.g. hitting a real route through FastAPI's TestClient once one is added, rather than calling get_ibkr_provider() directly) would mutate the plain module attribute via application code's own `global` assignment -- monkeypatch's teardown only reverts changes made through monkeypatch itself, not a later in-process `global` mutation, so such a test could leak a stale IBKRProvider (bound to a previous test's base_url/mock client) into later tests in the same pytest session, non-deterministically depending on execution order. Consider an autouse fixture in tests/unit/api/test_dependencies.py (or conftest.py) that resets the singleton to None on teardown. Found during PR #190's re-review.

decisions.decision: Replaced the `@lru_cache(maxsize=1)`-wrapped `_get_ibkr_provider_singleton()` (PR #191's own earlier fix, which pr-reviewer's needs_work review correctly flagged as not actually thread-safe) with an explicit `threading.Lock`-guarded double-checked-locking construction: a module-level `_ibkr_provider_singleton: IBKRProvider | None` global plus `_ibkr_provider_singleton_lock`, checked outside the lock (fast path once set), then re-checked inside the lock before constructing. Added a dedicated `_reset_ibkr_provider_singleton_for_tests()` helper (also lock-guarded) replacing the old `_get_ibkr_provider_singleton.cache_clear()` calls in tests/unit/api/test_dependencies.py's autouse fixture. Added a new regression test, `test_concurrent_first_requests_construct_only_one_singleton`, that races 32 threads (synchronized via a `threading.Barrier` so they call the getter as close to simultaneously as possible) against a cold singleton via `concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor` and asserts every thread got back the exact same (`is`-identical) instance.
decisions.rationale: This is exactly the fix pr-reviewer's needs_work comment asked for. Verified the new test actually catches the regression it's meant to catch (not just a test that happens to pass either way): temporarily reverted the getter to a lock-free check-then-set with an injected `time.sleep(0.01)` to widen the race window (simulating the old broken lru_cache-era behavior), confirmed the new concurrency test failed deterministically against that broken version (non-identical instances returned across threads), then restored the fixed lock-based implementation and confirmed the test passes reliably (10 consecutive runs, no flakes). A hand-rolled spin-lock or `queue`-based approach was considered and rejected as unnecessary complexity over the standard double-checked-locking idiom with `threading.Lock`, which is the textbook fix for exactly this race and was also pr-reviewer's own explicit suggestion.

decisions.decision: Both non-blocking checklist items were fixed directly on PR #190's branch (task/backend-ibkr-data-provider) while addressing that PR's needs_work blocking findings, rather than through a separate branch/PR of this task's own. state is deliberately left as 'planned' rather than flipped to 'done' here.
decisions.rationale: pr-reviewer's original review comment explicitly invited fixing these 'if convenient since you're already in this area' as part of resolving the two blocking findings on the same branch -- doing so avoids a near-duplicate PR re-touching the same two files (app/api/dependencies.py, docs/architecture/Backend.md) moments later. state is left as 'planned' (not flipped to 'done') because moving a task to done -- including the git mv into docs/tasks/done/ -- is documented as pr-reviewer's/pr-merger's call once a PR is actually reviewed and merged, not task-worker's to make unilaterally; pr-reviewer re-reviewing PR #190 will see both checklist items already checked and the actual diff (get_ibkr_provider now a process-wide singleton; Backend.md §3's httpx row updated) and can move this task to done in that same pass once PR #190 merges.

decisions.decision: Replaced app.api.dependencies's plain-module-global `_ibkr_provider_singleton` + hand-rolled `if ... is None:` check-then-set with a new private `@lru_cache(maxsize=1)`-wrapped factory function `_get_ibkr_provider_singleton()` that `get_ibkr_provider()` now calls instead of touching a global directly. Updated tests/unit/api/test_dependencies.py's two tests that previously did `monkeypatch.setattr("app.api.dependencies._ibkr_provider_singleton", None)` to no longer need that (the module global no longer exists), and added a new `_reset_ibkr_provider_singleton` autouse pytest fixture in that same file that calls `_get_ibkr_provider_singleton.cache_clear()` before and after every test in the module.
decisions.rationale: This is exactly the fix the checklist item itself suggested (an lru_cache-wrapped factory matching get_settings()'s already-thread-safe pattern in app/config.py), so no alternative was seriously considered -- a hand-rolled threading.Lock double-checked-locking implementation was rejected as reinventing what functools.lru_cache already provides for a zero-argument factory. The autouse fixture placement (test_dependencies.py itself, not a shared conftest.py) mirrors this module's existing pattern of ad hoc get_settings().cache_clear() calls scattered through its own tests rather than centralizing them, since no other test module in the suite currently touches get_ibkr_provider/the IBKR singleton -- if a future test elsewhere in the suite needs the same reset (e.g. an integration test hitting a route that consumes get_ibkr_provider), it should move to a shared conftest.py fixture at that point rather than pre-emptively generalizing here for a need that doesn't exist yet. Verified: full backend test suite (890 tests), ruff, and mypy all pass on the changed files; the pre-existing ruff/mypy findings elsewhere in the backend tree (tests/unit/indicators/test_stochastic.py, tests/unit/signals/test_triple_screen.py, several tests/integration/*.py untyped-def/arg-type findings) were confirmed present on main before this change and are unrelated to this task's scope.

comments.summary: Re-review of the needs_work fix. `_get_ibkr_provider_singleton()` (app/api/dependencies.py:52-85) now uses genuine double-checked locking: fast-path read outside the lock, `with _ibkr_provider_singleton_lock:` re-check-then-construct inside it, global reassigned only after `IBKRProvider(...)` is fully constructed. Traced this by hand against CPython's actual semantics (GIL serializes STORE_GLOBAL/LOAD_GLOBAL, so no partially-constructed instance can ever be observed by another thread) -- correct, no TOCTOU gap. `_reset_ibkr_provider_singleton_for_tests()` goes through the same lock, so a reset can't race a concurrent construction either.

Independently verified the new concurrency test is a reliable, non-flaky regression check rather than a test that could pass by luck: `thread_count=32` matches `ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=32)` so all 32 submitted tasks get real worker threads, and `threading.Barrier(32)` blocks every thread until all 32 have arrived before any calls `_get_ibkr_provider_singleton()` -- this does genuinely force simultaneous arrival at the check, not just interleaved-but-staggered calls. Ran it 30 times against the fixed implementation (0 failures). Then reproduced the task-worker's own claimed verification myself: temporarily patched the getter back to a lock-free check-then-set with an injected `time.sleep(0.01)` (widening the race window) and reran the test 5 times -- failed deterministically every time (distinct `is`-identities returned across threads), confirming the test actually catches the regression it targets rather than being a tautology. Restored the fix afterward; ruff/mypy clean.

Test-reset helper usage confirmed correct: the autouse fixture in test_dependencies.py (before+after every test in the module) is the only place in the tree that touches `_ibkr_provider_singleton`/`get_ibkr_provider` besides app code itself -- grepped the full backend tree and confirmed no other test file or route reaches this dependency yet, so no cross-test leak risk and the module-local (not conftest.py) fixture scope remains the right call, per the task's own decisions entry.

review.notes: Full backend suite: 891 passed, 99.93% coverage (well above the 90% gate). ruff and mypy clean on the changed files and the full backend tree (the only ruff findings anywhere are the same 7 pre-existing ones in test_stochastic.py/test_triple_screen.py already confirmed present on main and outside this diff's two touched files -- backend/app/api/dependencies.py, backend/tests/unit/api/test_dependencies.py). Frontend suite run for completeness even though this PR touches zero frontend files: 672 passed on a clean run (99.64% statement coverage); one earlier run showed a single timeout flake in PortfolioPage.test.tsx's 'adds a new position end to end' test under coverage-instrumented load, which passed both in isolation and on a full clean rerun -- a pre-existing, unrelated-to-this-diff flake, not tracked as a followup here since it has nothing to do with the IBKR provider area this task covers. No API route/schema touched, so no openapi.json regen needed (confirmed no diff). No UI surface in this PR (backend-only singleton fix, no route yet consumes get_ibkr_provider) -- browser walkthrough and the persisted e2e suite (steps 9/9a) are not applicable and were skipped accordingly. area is backend/data (not backend/signals or backend/portfolio) and skill is null, so verify-elder-signal doesn't apply; no new module/dependency/layer added (threading is stdlib), so architecture-review doesn't apply either. All three of the original review's blocking-fix asks were independently re-verified myself (not just re-read from the PR's own claims): (1) the lock-based implementation is genuinely correct, (2) the new concurrency test is genuinely reliable and does catch the regression -- reproduced the broken-then-fixed cycle myself rather than trusting the task-worker's account, (3) the reset fixture has no leak risk. No blocking findings; no non-blocking findings either. Accepting.

pr_decision.notes: Independently re-ran the full backend suite (891 passed, 99.93% coverage, matches pr-reviewer). Ran test_concurrent_first_requests_construct_only_one_singleton 15 times standalone with zero flakes, then myself reproduced the broken-vs-fixed cycle: patched _get_ibkr_provider_singleton to a lock-free check-then-set with an injected time.sleep(0.01), got 5/5 deterministic failures, restored the real fix from a backup copy and confirmed the diff was clean and all 6 tests in that module pass again. Read app/api/dependencies.py's double-checked locking by hand: fast-path read outside the lock, re-check inside the lock, global reassigned only after IBKRProvider(...) fully constructs -- correct under CPython's GIL (no torn/partial-object write is observable), no TOCTOU gap. Confirmed ruff/mypy clean using the project's actual configured invocations (bare `mypy`, scoped by pyproject.toml's `files = ["app"]`, and `ruff check .`) -- an initial explicit `mypy app/api/dependencies.py tests/...` run flagged pre-existing untyped-test-def findings, but that was my own invocation bypassing the config's file scope, not a real regression; the standard invocation is clean, matching pr-reviewer's claim.
